item.text:
**5B.8 Research Note**
Bottom line: **mixed, leaning no on actual fair distribution, though there is real evidence of broad-based, non-elite-targeted program design**. The government backed visible investments in rural connectivity, safety nets, education, health, WASH, refugees/IDPs, and conflict-affected areas. But the 2024 record also shows severe regional exclusion from violence, aid diversion, and emergency-rule coercion, especially in Amhara and among displaced or conflict-affected groups.

- **World Bank backs inclusive growth reforms**
  - **Publisher:** World Bank
  - **Date:** 2024-07-30
  - **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth
  - **Claim:** The reform package explicitly aimed at a more inclusive economy, stronger social safety nets, better fiscal transparency, and improved public spending effectiveness. That is positive evidence of an equity-oriented distributional agenda, not a narrow supporter-only payoff.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.5

- **Rural connectivity program targets all regions and half women**
  - **Publisher:** World Bank
  - **Date:** 2024-03-29
  - **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/29/ethiopia-afe-world-bank-helps-strengthen-rural-connectivity-and-road-access-to-boost-climate-resilience-food-security
  - **Claim:** The program was designed to improve rural market access across all 13 regions and said 50% of the 11.3 million intended beneficiaries were women. This is strong positive evidence for geographically and gender-inclusive distribution.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Finance ministry says the 1.72 billion USD package funded public goods**
  - **Publisher:** Ethiopia Ministry of Finance
  - **Date:** 2024-04-05
  - **URL:** https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/
  - **Claim:** The agreements funded rural connectivity, adaptive safety nets, food security, and other development projects aimed at sustainable and inclusive growth. That supports a reading of broad public-good allocation rather than favoring regime insiders.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6, 5B.5

- **Education gains were targeted to disadvantaged regions, girls, and refugees**
  - **Publisher:** World Bank
  - **Date:** 2024-09-05
  - **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia
  - **Claim:** The education program reported improved girls’ enrollment in historically disadvantaged regions and support for refugee schools, female teachers, tablets, and training. That is direct evidence of distribution toward groups often left behind.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Health and WASH investments reached girls, schools, and conflict-affected communities**
  - **Publisher:** World Bank
  - **Date:** 2024-01-19
  - **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/01/19/breaking-barriers-empowering-girls-with-clean-water-and-sanitation-facilities-in-ethiopias-schools
  - **Claim:** The school WASH program expanded sanitation access and improved attendance, especially for girls. This supports a fair-distribution reading because it targets a basic service gap that disproportionately harms poorer households and girls.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **GBV services expanded across five conflict-affected regions**
  - **Publisher:** World Bank
  - **Date:** 2024-10-11
  - **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/10/11/gender-based-violence-gbv-response-services-in-afe-ethiopia-empowering-women-and-girls-in-conflict-affected-areas
  - **Claim:** The project supported access to GBV response services across Afar, Amhara, Benshangul-Gumz, Oromia, and Tigray for about 5 million people. This is good evidence of gender- and region-sensitive allocation.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Refugee/IDP inclusion was explicitly built into 2024 programming**
  - **Publisher:** UNICEF Ethiopia
  - **Date:** 2024-03-21
  - **URL:** https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host
  - **Claim:** The PROSPECTS partnership aimed to strengthen resilience, self-reliance, and inclusion for refugees, IDPs, and host communities through education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure. This is positive evidence against a regime-support-only allocation pattern.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Tigray reconstruction restored schools, health facilities, and WASH**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations in Ethiopia
  - **Date:** 2024-02-23
  - **URL:** https://ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray
  - **Claim:** The project reconstructed 14 health centers, 11 schools, and 33 WASH facilities for 365,000 people in five woredas. That is strong positive evidence of rebuilding in a war-affected region rather than concentrating gains only in the center.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Refugees in Amhara were protected by a new site, but only after conflict disruption**
  - **Publisher:** UNHCR Africa
  - **Date:** 2024-08-28
  - **URL:** https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-s-refugees-and-returnees-service-and-unhcr-establish-new-site-host-sudanese-refugees-fleeing-unrest
  - **Claim:** Ethiopia and UNHCR opened a new site with better security, food, water, sanitation, medical aid, and protection for Sudanese refugees. This shows some corrective redistribution to vulnerable groups, but it also underscores that displacement from conflict was already shaping who got access.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6

- **Aid diversion and loss of access hit the most vulnerable hardest**
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 2024-01-12
  - **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia
  - **Claim:** HRW reported that WFP and USAID halted food aid after a widespread, coordinated diversion scheme, and the suspension severely restricted food access for about 20 million people, especially in displacement and refugee camps. That is strong negative evidence for fair distribution in practice.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.5, 5B.6

- **Amhara emergency and mass arrests show unequal treatment across regions and groups**
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 2024-04-04
  - **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region
  - **Claim:** HRW documented summary executions in Amhara and described an abusive conflict environment under federal forces. Even if not a fiscal distribution story in itself, it is strong evidence that some regions were being treated as coercive security zones rather than equal beneficiaries of state protection and economic inclusion.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6, 5B.5

- **State of emergency deepened exclusion of Amhara residents**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters, republished by KELO
  - **Date:** 2024-02-02
  - **URL:** https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/
  - **Claim:** Parliament extended emergency rule after heavy fighting and abuse allegations. That is negative context for fair distribution because the government’s response relied on coercive control in a region where civilians were already bearing the costs.
  - **Questions:** 5B.8; also 5B.6, 5B.5

**Search gap**
- I found **strong evidence of inclusive program design** in infrastructure, safety nets, education, health, refugee support, and gender-targeted services.
- I found **much weaker direct evidence that Abiy personally allocated economic gains evenly across supporters and non-supporters**. Most positive items are project-level and partner-supported, not proof of political neutrality.
- I found **strong negative evidence that conflict and emergency rule produced unequal access** for Amhara civilians, refugees, IDPs, and other vulnerable groups.
- I did **not** find clean 2024 evidence of a systematic patronage scheme in the economic-distribution sense, but the overall pattern still looks **uneven and conflict-skewed rather than fairly distributed**.
